samuel1.18.p1.b1.text: After David had finished speaking with Saul, the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together, and Jonathan loved him as himself.

samuel1.18.p1.b2.text: And from that day Saul kept David with him and did not let him return to his father’s house.

samuel1.18.p1.b3.text: And Jonathan removed the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, his sword, his bow, and his belt.

samuel1.18.p2.b1.text: … Saul set him over the men of war. And this was pleasing in the sight of all the people, and of Saul’s officers as well.

samuel1.18.p2.b2.text: … the women came out of all the cities of Israel to meet King Saul with singing and dancing, with joyful songs, and with tambourines and other instruments.

samuel1.18.p2.b3.text: Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.

samuel1.18.p3.b1.text: They have ascribed tens of thousands to David … but only thousands to me. What more can he have but the kingdom?

samuel1.18.p3.b2.text: And from that day forward Saul kept a jealous eye on David.

samuel1.18.p4.b1.text: The next day a spirit of distress sent from God came upon Saul, and he prophesied inside the house …

samuel1.18.p4.b2.text: … while David played the harp as usual. Now Saul was holding a spear,

samuel1.18.p4.b3.text: I will pin David to the wall.

samuel1.18.p5.b1.text: So Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with David but had departed from Saul.

samuel1.18.p5.b2.text: Therefore Saul sent David away and gave him command of a thousand men. David led the troops out to battle and back,

samuel1.18.p5.b3.text: When Saul saw that David was very successful, he was afraid of him.

samuel1.18.p5.b4.text: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he was leading them out to battle and back.

samuel1.18.p6.b1.text: Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you in marriage. Only be valiant for me and fight the LORD’s battles.

samuel1.18.p6.b2.text: I need not raise my hand against him; let the hand of the Philistines be against him.

samuel1.18.p6.b3.text: Who am I, and what is my family or my father’s clan in Israel, that I should become the son-in-law of the king?

samuel1.18.p6.b4.text: So when it was time to give Saul’s daughter Merab to David, she was given in marriage to Adriel of Meholah.

samuel1.18.p7.b1.text: Now Saul’s daughter Michal loved David, and when this was reported to Saul, it pleased him.

samuel1.18.p7.b2.text: I will give her to David … so that she may be a snare to him, and the hand of the Philistines may be against him.

samuel1.18.p7.b3.text: Behold, the king is pleased with you, and all his servants love you. Now therefore, become his son-in-law.

samuel1.18.p7.b4.text: Does it seem trivial in your sight to be the son-in-law of the king? I am a poor man and lightly esteemed.

samuel1.18.p8.b1.text: Say to David, ‘The king desires no other dowry but a hundred Philistine foreskins as revenge on his enemies.’

samuel1.18.p8.b2.text: But Saul intended to cause David’s death at the hands of the Philistines. … he was pleased to become the king’s son-in-law.

samuel1.18.p8.b3.text: David and his men went out and killed two hundred Philistines. … to become the king’s son-in-law.

samuel1.18.p8.b4.text: Then Saul gave his daughter Michal to David in marriage.

samuel1.18.p9.b1.text: When Saul realized that the LORD was with David and that his daughter Michal loved David,

samuel1.18.p9.b2.text: he grew even more afraid of David. So from then on Saul was David’s enemy.

samuel1.18.p9.b3.text: Every time the Philistine commanders came out for battle, David was more successful than all of Saul’s officers, so that his name was highly esteemed.
